page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-64xCPU-512GB is a Cloud Native family server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The system provides 64 vCPUs mapped to 64 physical cores with a single thread per core under a shared CPU allocation model. It is equipped with 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. This configuration does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals distinct performance tradeoffs. Single-core processing is limited, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance ranking in the bottom 10%. However, the high core count enables strong multi-threaded capabilities. Passmark CPU, extended instructions, encryption, and physics tests all register in the top 25%. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench ray tracing also perform in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth remains average across both small and large block reads and writes, while Redis SET operations demonstrate strong throughput at 67.51 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the shared CPU allocation model offers a high density of memory and cores at a lower hardware tier relative to dedicated resources. This makes the server suitable for memory-intensive workloads that can tolerate shared CPU scheduling. Recommended workloads include large-scale in-memory caching via Redis, multi-threaded data decompression, and parallel batch processing. It is less suited for latency-sensitive single-threaded applications or local storage-heavy databases due to the lack of bundled local disks.
